statement: Display important information in lists, callout boxes, tables and illustrations.

anchor.quote: Display important information in lists, callout boxes, tables and illustrations.

tags.specification: Treat the named formats as available ways to display important information, not a requirement to repeat every important point in all four formats. Importance depends on the content and user purpose.
tags.violation_condition: Important information is left only in ordinary running prose rather than displayed in a list, callout box, table or illustration.

when: When presenting important information.
view.why: G-2: the named presentation forms are alternatives within one information-presentation check.

statement: Structure your content by writing about one idea at a time:

anchor.quote: Structure your content by writing about one idea at a time:

tags.specification: Interpret this as developing ideas in turn rather than repeatedly switching between unfinished ideas. It does not specify one idea per sentence or per paragraph.
tags.violation_condition: The development of separate ideas is interleaved, with the text repeatedly leaving an unfinished idea to develop another and then returning to it.

when: When developing multiple ideas in content.
view.why: The lead-in states a textual property distinct from the following checks on priority, grouping, length and order.

statement: Start with the most important idea first.

anchor.quote: Start with the most important idea first.

tags.specification: Assess the opening idea of the content being structured. Importance is judged against the user's purpose; the page gives no mechanical ranking or instruction to apply this separately to every paragraph.
tags.violation_condition: Less important ideas precede the most important idea at the start of the content.

when: When arranging the ideas in content.
view.why: This checks the placement of the leading idea, rather than the existence of a hierarchy or topical grouping.

anchor.quote: Group related ideas under headings.

tags.violation_condition: Related ideas are not collected into a topical group under a heading.

when: When organising related ideas in content.
view.why: This checks topical grouping under headings, separately from heading wording and hierarchy.

statement: Organise ideas into short paragraphs.

anchor.quote: Organise ideas into short paragraphs.

tags.specification: The page does not define short. A paragraph-length criterion needs reviewer agreement; no word or sentence threshold is inferred here.
tags.violation_condition: Ideas are packed into an overlong paragraph rather than divided into short paragraphs.

when: When presenting ideas in prose paragraphs.
view.why: E-4: retain the paragraph-length requirement without inventing a numerical definition of short.

statement: Make sure ideas flow from one paragraph to the next.

anchor.quote: Make sure ideas flow from one paragraph to the next.

tags.specification: Assess whether successive paragraphs have an intelligible progression of ideas. Explicit transition words are not required when the relationship is already clear.
tags.violation_condition: Successive paragraphs have an incoherent progression or an abrupt, unexplained jump between ideas.

when: When content contains successive paragraphs.
view.why: This checks progression between paragraphs, distinct from the order of sentences within a paragraph.

statement: Use a logical order for sentences.

anchor.quote: Use a logical order for sentences.

tags.specification: Assess whether sentence order supports the progression and dependencies of the ideas. Several different orders may be logical.
tags.violation_condition: The order of sentences disrupts the logical progression of the ideas.

when: When arranging multiple sentences in prose.
view.why: This is the sentence-order check, not a second finding for paragraph-to-paragraph flow.
